title: 24.3: A PVT-Robust 2×Interleaved 2.2GS/s ADC with Gated-CCRO-Based Quantizer Shared Across Channels and Steps Achieving >4.5GHz ERBW
problem: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based ADCs offer compact, scaling-friendly designs but face challenges: VC-RO requires nonlinear tuning calibration and individual ROs per sub-channel; gated-RO shares poorly across channels due to long integer-counting; cyclic coupled ROs have phase errors. Achieving high energy/area efficiency with multi-channel interleaving remains difficult.
motivation: DSP-based wireline communication demands medium-resolution GS/s ADCs with high energy and area efficiency for massive interleaving to increase throughput while maintaining PVT robustness.
method: A 2×64-channel time-interleaved two-step ADC uses a gated cyclic coupled ring-oscillator (G-CCRO) based quantizer shared across both channels and conversion steps. The G-CCRO operates independently of sampled input amplitude with inherent phase interpolation, while the ramp generator is reallocated to the reference path (vs. input path) to maintain constant input impedance and reduce kickback.
key_novelty: Shared gated-CCRO quantizer enabling efficient channel/step interleaving with inherent phase interpolation and constant input impedance.
contributions: 2.2GS/s operation with 2× channel interleaving and 2-step conversion sharing
Shared G-CCRO quantizer across channels and steps improving energy/area efficiency
PVT-robust design with constant input path impedance
7b ENOB at 4.5GHz input, 19.7fJ/conv-step Walden FoM, 0.004mm² core area
baselines: Prior VC-RO ADCs (requires calibration, individual RO per channel)
Gated-RO ADCs (difficult channel sharing, long integer-counting)
limitations: Not discussed; temperature/voltage/process stability margins, noise performance, and dynamic range over process corners not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Shared G-CCRO quantizer for interleaved ADCs
